# No Family Is an Island — Study Companion

> A single-page study aid by Curtis Hoffmann for Ilana Gershon's ethnography No Family Is an Island: Cultural Expertise among Samoans in Diaspora (Cornell University Press, 2012), built as a companion for an anthropology course with the Introduction and Chapters 1 to 4 in focus. Distant reading (concept and relationship maps) beside close reading (a chapter-by-chapter guide and scene-level commentary). The book is in copyright and is not reproduced; the guides are original summaries.

Site: https://curtishoffmann.com/samoan-culture/
Source: https://github.com/phagehunter/samoan-culture

## Four views

- Study / Exam: the book in one idea, the central Ben-versus-Alofa clash (systems carrier versus cultural broker), the cultural/acultural contrast, every starred term grouped by domain, a chapter-by-chapter nutshell.
- Key Terms: a force-directed concept map of Gershon's analytic terms plus the Samoan and bureaucratic terms the argument turns on; a gold ring marks key terms.
- People and Systems: who meets whom across families and chiefs, churches, government bureaucracies and the community brokers between them; red dashed edges mark a clash of reflexivities; node size by degree centrality.
- Narrative Gravity: a stream graph of what each section attends to (families, churches, systems, brokers, theory), with the focus window marked and a setting strip (US, New Zealand, Samoa).

## Controls and data

- Section slider (Introduction to Conclusion), group toggles, playback, commentary panel with summaries, thematic tags and page citations linking into the Guide tab.
- Data are TypeScript constants in `src/data/`; guides are static per-section JSON in `public/text/`. No backend, no API keys, no map, one URL.
- Focalization percentages and interaction weights are editorial estimates. Personal names are Gershon's own, mostly pseudonyms.
